claim: WHO ( World Health Organization) approved water, salt and vinegar remedy for coronavirus
justification: Multiple high-confidence evidence items from both fact-checks, such as statements with confidence scores of 0.90 and 0.95, consistently confirm that the World Health Organization (WHO) never approved a water, salt, and vinegar remedy for COVID-19. WHO's official guidance, including Myth Busters pages and Director-General statements, emphasized no specific medicines for prevention or treatment and actively warned against unproven home remedies, while promoting evidence-based measures like handwashing and vaccination. Sources claiming WHO approval are assessed as originating from non-credible or fabricated contexts, reinforcing the refutation of the claim.
